title: Seqrite reports CLoader bot campaign using LuaJIT against organizations and individuals in Thailand
date_note: Seqrite's blog post is dated 23 November 2026 and gives no earlier day for the campaign.
geo_basis: country (Thailand) as stated by Seqrite; capital coordinates
summary: Seqrite Labs says it found a CLoader bot campaign targeting organizations and individuals in Thailand through spear-phishing emails. According to Seqrite, an archive disguised as a PDF holds obfuscated JavaScript that drops a LuaJIT executable and an obfuscated Lua script, which contact command servers and install the bot. Seqrite does not attribute the campaign to a named group or country.
plain: Security firm Seqrite says phishing emails are delivering a bot program called CLoader to people and organizations in Thailand. The firm names no group behind it.
exec: Seqrite reports a phishing-delivered bot campaign aimed at Thai organizations and individuals.
action: Seqrite's post lists indicators of compromise (file hashes, IP addresses, domains) and the detection name Trojan.AgentCiR; check your systems against them.

validation.note: Only Seqrite's own research post was read; no independent publisher reports it and no victim has commented.

review.note: Compared date, targets, delivery chain, no attribution, detection name against Seqrite post
